headline: Software Engineer · Lead Mobile Developer at
bio: I work across mobile, web and native systems, from building products from scratch to optimizing performance-critical code.

At Neutune I built the iOS and Android app from an empty repository and now lead its development, and I build its web applications. I've had C++ performance work merged into one of Software Mansion's React Native libraries, and I write my own open-source tools for diagnosing performance and stability problems in React Native and Android apps.
Previously I was the founding engineer at WWBW. I studied Computer Science at UNIST.

mixaudio.tagline: Play songs and remake them by chatting with an AI that rearranges the stems
mixaudio.summary: MixAudio lets people play songs and remixes and remake them by asking an AI agent to rearrange the individual instrument tracks, on the web and on phones. I started the iOS and Android app from an empty repo, wrote most of it and shipped it to 0.9.0; on the web I own the player, the queue and the studio's track grid.

parts.label: iOS & Android
highlights: Stopped playback crashing on busy songs. On a Galaxy S21 the native render thread was running at 94–160% of a core; I shared clip buffers instead of copying each stem, added fast paths for settled parameters and moved output off an underrunning low-latency stream. In on-device profiling, a 16-stem, 3-minute mix with heavy effects now renders at 60–65% of one core.

Patched the react-native-audio-api engine in C++: a two-stage convolver for reverb, a feedback-delay node, separate output buffers for nodes with several consumers, and a shared worklet runtime that fixed a crash.

Ported the web reverb, delay and Signalsmith time-stretch to native nodes, with parity checks against Chrome: reverb and delay at zero lag and a residual of -60 dB or lower, time-stretch spectra within -50 dB.
Cut process CPU by about 35% and JS-thread CPU by 30% while stems load on a Galaxy S21.
Made the feed and players smoother: streamed playback instead of decoding whole files, covers drawn off the JS thread with Skia, and a progress bar that no longer redraws the screen every frame.

parts.label: Web
highlights: Cut time to first sound by up to 9×: playback starts once the first second of every stem has loaded. On Fast 4G a 13-stem song went from 3.65 s to 1.78 s, and a 23-stem, 10 MB project from 13 s to 1.41 s.
Removed the freeze on every mute and solo: loudness is now measured in cancellable time slices, cached by what's rendered and reused on undo.
Virtualized the studio's track grid in both directions, with one shared context menu and tooltip per grid and full keyboard navigation that snaps to clip and section edges.
Built the player, queue, up-next panel and workspace bottom player.

neusynth.tagline: AI sample-generation plugin for music software (VST3 / AU)
neusynth.summary: A plugin that generates audio samples with AI inside music software such as Cubase and Logic. I've worked on it since v0.1.
highlights: Built musical key detection in C++ from scratch, with a benchmark tool that scores it the way the MIREX research evaluations do.
Added native crash reporting inside DAW hosts. Because the plugin shares a process with the host, reports keep only the plugin's own stack frames, computed at startup to avoid a loader-lock deadlock.
Recovered generations interrupted by a dropped connection, and added audio trimming and context range selection.
Connected the C++ engine to the Vue interface, and led the redesigned V2 interface and its component system.
Added saving, searching, favoriting and reloading of generated audio.
Cut the landing page's animated background from about 120 ms to 9 ms per frame with pixel-identical output, and added English and Korean localization.
Fixed Cubase integration and the macOS release process.

tenant.tagline: Web apps for managing a music catalog and working with artists
tenant.summary: A set of internal and partner web apps for running a music catalog.
highlights: Designed and built the Tagger app on my own: people mark song sections directly on the audio waveform.
Built artist analytics, track performance dashboards and the flow for submitting new works.
Built reporting and usage analytics pages for the admin app.
Built chart components shared across several apps.

thounds.summary: A music-creation app built jointly by Neutune and Blooming Grace. I designed it from scratch and led its development.
highlights: Designed the app architecture, state management and UI system.
Built an audio engine that plays multiple stems in sync, each with its own controls.
Implemented waveform display and punch-in recording at any position on the timeline.
Shipped the core workflows and audio features to production.

react-native-audio-api.tagline: Software Mansion's audio engine for React Native
react-native-audio-api.summary: A performance feature and several fixes merged into the native C++ core of Software Mansion's React Native audio engine.
highlights: Rebuilt the convolver as a two-stage partitioned convolver that computes long reverb tails on worker threads, cutting incremental reverb cost 8.8× (922M to 105M cycles per second) on a Galaxy S21 with output identical to the original.
Fixed Android output-stream sharing, looping in AudioBufferSourceNode, start() duration timing and true-stereo convolution gain.

thread-inspector.tagline: A local flight recorder for React Native freezes
thread-inspector.summary: When the JS or main thread stalls in a release build, it saves an incident: what was running, how sure it is, and a trace you can open in Perfetto. Nothing leaves the device.
highlights: Lock-free C++ recorder shared by iOS and Android: one fixed-size ring per thread, 64-byte events, 32–48 ns per event on a Galaxy S21.
Cut idle overhead on a Galaxy S21 from 1.7% to 0.6% of one core, meeting my 1% goal, by having the watchdog probe idle threads less often.
A watchdog probes the JS and main queues every 100 ms, backing off to 500 ms for idle threads, and snapshots the last 5 seconds of history the moment a stall starts.
Each finding states its evidence (direct containment, explicit flow, or temporal overlap only) and reports unattributed time instead of guessing.
Opt-in adapters for Fabric commits, TurboModule calls, React Navigation, Android frame timings and Hermes stack sampling with source-map symbolication; JS stacks can be saved with every incident.
Per-thread CPU profiling and, on Android, context-switch counts, plus a CLI that pulls incidents from Android devices, iOS simulators and iPhones, then merges and compares them.
Core tested under AddressSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer, with 21 C++ and 7 CLI tests. Overhead measured on a real device with paired runs and bootstrap confidence intervals.

adrive.tagline: CLI and MCP server for driving and diagnosing Android apps over adb
adrive.summary: A small CLI and MCP server that reads and drives installed Android apps, including release builds with looping animations or live audio meters, where UiAutomator-based tools stall waiting for idle.
highlights: Reads the accessibility tree without ever waiting for idle: on an animating screen on a Galaxy S21 it answers in 0.10–0.15 s after the first call, where uiautomator dump fails and maestro hierarchy takes 5 s.
adrive mcp serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio for Claude Code, Cursor and other clients; screenshots come back as images.
Installs nothing on the device: a small dex runs from /data/local/tmp with shell privileges.
Diagnoses release builds: CPU per thread, memory and frame jank, audio underruns and buffer sizes, crashes and per-process logs.
adrive run measures a scenario step by step (frames, jank, CPU per thread, memory) and can record a Perfetto trace.
Plain text for people, --json for scripts and AI agents; no npm dependencies. CI runs it on emulators for API 26 to 36.

lazymobile.tagline: MCP server for agent-driven mobile QA
lazymobile.summary: Proposed the first MCP tool surface for the project and worked through the design with its maintainer.
highlights: Device control, app lifecycle, bounded logs, screenshots and the safety boundaries around them.

highlights: Built a multi-agent AI ordering system that reads both text and images.
Shipped the cross-platform B2B app for iOS and Android with Flutter and JavaScript.
Added image optimization and PDF/Excel export.

article.title: What a React Native freeze recorder can prove
article.subtitle: A case study in building a local flight recorder for React Native, and in being honest about where its evidence runs out.
points: Detecting a stall is easy; that "easy" part still hid two bugs.
Attribution needs explicit relations, not just time overlap.
React Native internals limit what can be observed.
The idle overhead comes from watchdog probing, not recording.
